# relnotes

**Release notes from git history, generated by an open-weight model.**

`relnotes` reads your git log and rewrites it into a short, plain-English
changelog for end users — the thing you keep forgetting to write before you
tag a release. It talks to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint backed by an
open-weight model (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM) and falls back to a
deterministic template when no model is reachable, so it never blocks your
release pipeline.

Built for the [Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge: Week 2 — Side Hustle](https://dev.to/challenges/hf26).

## Why open weights

- **Zero per-release cost.** It runs on a 3B model on your laptop. A hosted
  API would charge you to summarise text you already own.
- **Your commit history never leaves the machine.** Commit messages leak
  internal project names, unreleased features, and occasionally a pasted
  secret. Local inference keeps the diff on your side of the wire.
- **No vendor lock-in.** Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works. Change model
  without changing code.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Mystical89/relnotes
cd relnotes
./relnotes.py --offline --since v1.2.0   # no model needed
```

Python 3.10+, no dependencies.

## Usage

```bash
# with an open-weight model (default: Ollama at localhost:11434)
relnotes.py --since v1.2.0

# deterministic template only — fast, offline, CI-safe
relnotes.py --since v1.2.0 --offline

# point at any OpenAI-compatible server
relnotes.py --since v1.2.0 \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 \
  --model qwen2.5:3b

# write straight to your release notes file
relnotes.py --since v1.2.0 -o RELEASE_NOTES.md
```

### Recognising your commits

Plain subjects land under **Changed**. Conventional Commits get placed
properly:

| Prefix | Section |
|---|---|
| `feat:` | Added |
| `fix:`, `revert:` | Fixed |
| `perf:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, `chore:` | Changed |

## Real output

`relnotes.py --offline` on this repository, after the README and skill commits:

```console
### Added

- initial CLI skeleton with offline template rendering

### Changed

- add README and relnotes agent skill
- cover conventional-commit parsing and CLI end to end
```

Note that `--since <root>` excludes the root commit itself (`root..HEAD`
semantics) — pass no `--since` to include everything.

## How it works

1. `git log` is collected between `--since` and `--until` (merges skipped).
2. If a model endpoint answers, commits go to it with a strict system prompt:
   group under Added/Fixed/Changed, ≤12 words per bullet, no hashes, no file
   names, no jargon. Temperature 0.3 for repeatability.
3. If the endpoint is down or `--offline` is set, the same grouping is done
   deterministically from Conventional Commits. The output shape is identical.
